claims.hypothesis: What are the dust spectral index and dust mass of the outer disk?
claims.experiment: Spectral index SED and maps from 0.87, 1.1 and 2.2 mm; optically thin dust mass with T=39 K

claims.finding: The disk has a typical spectral index of 2.3 and a small dust mass

evidence.quote: The protoplanetary disk has a typical spectral index of 2.3, computed using the 0.87, 1.1, and 2.2 mm bands.

claims.experiment: Contrast ratios from maps convolved to the NOEMA beam at 0.87, 1.1 and 2.2 mm

referee_caveats_inferred: The free-free fraction at 0.87 mm is 37% in the abstract but 31% in the Discussion
The 1.1 mm integrated flux is 108 mJy in Table 2 and Section 3.1 but 92 mJy in the conclusions; central-source spectral index is 1.1 in Section 3 but 1.0 in the conclusions
Contrast ratios from the ring maximum/minimum depend on beam convolution and noise; the claimed wavelength trend is not significant
Slab-model temperature is prior-dominated, so grain size and surface density depend on the fixed 39 K prior
Dust composition and opacity are assumed (DSHARP composition in the slab model, water ice and silicate in the RT), so dust masses and grain sizes are model-dependent
RT model uses a_max of 1 cm and different parameters than the slab fit, and matches contrast only qualitatively (synthetic 4.3 vs observed 3.1)
